newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian drug king complains of "unethical" slurs.
newsitem.headline: Colombian drug king complains of "unethical" slurs.

text.p: Colombia's billionaire cocaine king Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela has sent a letter from his jail cell complaining about "shame-faced and unethical" criticism of a judge who sentenced him to a light prison term.
In an indignant letter published in the Espectador newspaper on Wednesday, the former No. 2 of the mighty Cali drug cartel also denied claims he was plotting a jail break.

"I want to draw to your attention to the insidiousness of the media which have been putting shame-faced and unethical pressure on the regional judge who sentenced me, looking for a (heavier) sentence when it is not merited," Rodriguez wrote to the head of the National Prisons Institute, Col. Rafael Pardo.

Rodriguez and his brother Gilberto, the former cartel chief, were sentenced two weeks ago to terms that will in practice see them walk free in five years. They had confessed to heading a multi-billion-dollar criminal empire for more than 20 years and sending tonnes of cocaine across the globe.

The ruling sparked outrage from some Colombian politicians and condemnation by U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette and senior officials in U.S. President Bill Clinton's administration. Some officials suggested the judge had been bought off by the Cali cartel.

The controversy surrounding the brothers was compounded over the weekend by the leak of an anonymous letter to authorities at Bogota's La Picota prison, where the brothers are held, saying Miguel Rodriguez was planning to escape.
"Nothing could be more wrong and tendentious than that false piece of news. These unnamed sources are mounting a serious campaign against me," Rodriguez said in his letter.

Rodriguez may face further charges and a potentially longer spell behind bars if he is convicted of shipping 150 tonnes of cocaine to Tampa, Florida, and of offering a $1 million bribe to the judge handling the case.
